rationale: The plan correctly identifies the n=1-per-group design as unable to support any gene-level inference, refuses to run the Wald test, reports normalized counts and descriptive log2 fold changes only, and names the replicated design required for valid inference — the core requirement of the reference. QC is design-aware (library sizes, detected genes, sample distance, noting PCA is degenerate with two samples) though it lacks an explicit outlier/shallow-sample policy; filtering (>=10 counts in >=1 sample) and median-of-ratios normalization inside the model are minimal, justified, and correctly ordered. A technical flaw: apeglm lfcShrink depends on a fitted dispersion, and with zero residual degrees of freedom DESeq2 cannot estimate dispersion at all, so the shrinkage step as written is not executable — the plan asserts it without addressing this. The GSEA add-on is well specified (full ranked list, named collections, 15-500 size window, leading edge, BH), but it manufactures FDR-controlled pathway p-values from a single unreplicated fold-change ranking, which reintroduces inferential claims the design cannot support even with the hedging language; the reporting step is otherwise thorough on caveats, versions, and thresholds.
